subject: Re: Regulated vertical privacy — operational gaps & onshore fallbacks
content:
From: Sarah Owens <sarah.owens@harborhealth.org>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Brennan <tom.brennan@harborhealth.org>, HarborHealth Legal <legal@harborhealth.org>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Regulated deployment questions + request for operational gap playbook

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — HarborHealth is excited about Redwood but we need to validate a few operational constraints before moving to pilot. Legal flagged three areas that must be addressed for us to proceed to a scoped pilot:

- BAA coverage and uplifts required for our EHR-backed integrations (we need to confirm what counts as "process PHI" vs. metadata in your hosted API).
- Subprocessor locality: we require documented onshore fallbacks for any subprocessor that processes PHI or financial data; we also need the inventory and typical SLA for notification/transition.
- Cross-border transfers: we need a clear path if we must keep data in-region (US) and documentation for your EU->US transfer mechanisms for future sites.

Can you share an "operational gaps playbook" that maps Redwood's contractual DPA language to operational artifacts (SOC2, encryption attestations, KMS keys, subprocessor list, and runbooks for onshore failover)? We attached our initial redlines; happy to walk through.

Best,
Sarah
Director, Vendor Risk
HarborHealth

---

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Owens <sarah.owens@harborhealth.org>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Regulated deployment questions + request for operational gap playbook

Sarah — thanks for the clear list. I can pull together a playbook and map each redline to the operational artifact. Quick notes up front so we align expectations:

- BAA: Redwood supports BAA for hosted and private deployments. For hosted API customers, PHI classification is a customer responsibility, but our docs and field mapping examples clarify common patterns for EHR data. We will call out specific endpoints and storage locations where PHI could persist.

- Subprocessors: we maintain a canonical subprocessor inventory (attached) and a documented onshore fallback path that uses our US-only processing pools. For mission-critical PHI paths we can provide an architecture diagram and a runbook for automatic routing to the onshore tier.

- Cross-border transfers: we currently rely on standard contractual terms and SCC-equivalent controls for EU->US transfers, plus per-customer residency options via Redwood Private.

I'm looping in Vanessa (partnerships/enterprise) and Irene (security/compliance) to own the artifacts and walk you through specifics. I'll assemble a working playbook draft by Thursday COB and include: DPA redline commentary, SOC2 snapshot, KMS and encryption attestation, subprocessor inventory, and an onshore failover runbook.

Best,
Markus
Head of Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_snapshot_Q1.xlsx, subprocessor_inventory_2027-06.csv

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 08:56:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Regulated deployment questions + request for operational gap playbook

Thanks for the ping. Quick compliance read:

1) BAA redlines — HarborHealth asks for expanded subprocessing clause and stricter data classification obligations. We should push back on customer-mandated classification language; instead offer explicit examples and a customer attestation template.

2) Onshore fallback — we have a documented onboarding option that pins workloads to dedicated US pools; typical lead time 4–6 weeks for Dedicated or Redwood Private. For hosted (self-serve) we can provide an SLA-backed onshore tier for an additional monthly fee but require a capacity commit.

3) Subprocessor notifications — current contract gives 30 days notice and opt-out for high-risk subprocessors; HarborHealth asks for 14 days and immediate notification for PHI-related changes. Suggest counter-proposal: 21 days + 24-hour emergency notification window for PHI-impacting changes, plus a transitional runbook.

4) Evidence artifacts — I will attach a SOC2 snapshot and our KMS attestation. For GLBA-specific controls (financial ingestion), recommend we provide a short remediation checklist for their PCI/electronic-payments flow.

I will draft the playbook sections and a customer-facing one-pager with the counter-proposals by end of day tomorrow. Priyom, can you run cost/lead-time for the dedicated onshore tier and include a conservative estimate for provisioning and testing?

Irene
Sr. Security & Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_snapshot_Q1.xlsx, kms_attestation_2027-05.pdf

Cost/lead-time estimates:
- Dedicated US pool (4 GPUs, HA config) — provisioning + validation: 3 weeks; estimated incremental monthly price: $9,500.
- Redwood Private (customer-managed) — packaging + airgap options: 6–8 weeks; project fee + onboarding.
- Onshore hosted tier (SLA-backed routing) — available in 2 weeks with capacity commit; incremental monthly: $6,000.

I'll include checklist items: network peering, KMS key exchange steps, EHR schema whiteboard, and a runbook for traffic cutover.

Priyom
